compliance_notes.content:
General concept, in our own words: many states require insurers to
                        file proposed rates and rating plans with a state insurance regulator
                        before use, and some lines require prior approval rather than just
                        notification. This note is a simplified, generic description for
                        demonstration purposes -- it is not a summary of any specific Illinois
                        statute and must not be relied on for compliance purposes.

General concept, in our own words: many states set expectations around
                        how quickly an insurer must acknowledge a claim, investigate it, and
                        communicate a decision to the policyholder, with escalating requirements
                        if a claim is delayed or denied. This note is a generic illustration only
                        and is not a summary of Texas's actual claims-handling requirements.

General concept, in our own words: states commonly prohibit specific
                        unfair practices in claims handling, such as misrepresenting policy
                        provisions, failing to promptly investigate, or offering settlements
                        substantially lower than what a reasonable investigation supports. This
                        is a generic, illustrative description only, not a summary of any
                        specific California statute or regulation.

General concept, in our own words: health insurers and their business
                        associates that handle protected health information (PHI) are generally
                        expected to apply administrative, physical, and technical safeguards
                        (access controls, encryption, audit logging, breach notification
                        procedures), consistent with the general aims of HIPAA in the US.
                        This note is a simplified, generic overview for demonstration only --
                        see docs/INSURANCE_RAG_GUIDE.md's compliance section and consult
                        qualified compliance/privacy counsel for a real deployment.

General concept, in our own words: insurers are commonly expected to
                        retain policy, claims, and underwriting records for a defined minimum
                        period to support audits, disputes, and regulatory examinations, with
                        longer retention sometimes required for certain lines or records
                        involving minors. This is a generic illustration only; see
                        docs/INSURANCE_RAG_GUIDE.md's data retention section for a
                        non-authoritative discussion of the general concept.
